blockers.title: noFanoutWhen grants the control plane a translation exception at exactly the point the cited source forbids it, contradicting two adjacent fields
blockers.text: 'Provider-only in-band Cancel that is not a host cancellation event. Control plane does not translate it into supervision meaning except under the owning J-1 join.'
blockers.defect: The trailing clause 'except under the owning J-1 join' carves out a case in which the control plane MAY translate provider meaning into supervision meaning. No source grants that, and three texts refuse it - including two inside this same artifact.

measurement.file 02 lines 171-173 (source, verbatim): the control plane may decide supervision/fate only under the owning contract and cannot translate provider meaning to resolve a race.
measurement.scopeCollision: The source prohibition is scoped precisely TO RESOLVING A RACE. CPC v2's J-1 IS the race join (race: 'cancellation versus result'). The exception is therefore carved exactly where the prohibition bites, not at its margin.
measurement.CPC v2 J-1 rule ends: 'The owning contract then decides what a result-after-cancel or cancel-after-result IS.' - meaning assignment belongs to the owning contract, never to the control plane.
measurement.CPC v2 ID-DEP-2: 'RF-1..RF-8 and the J-1..J-5 orderings bind ORDERING and refusal-class identity only.'
measurement.selfContradiction1: $.t1CancellationComposition.composition.mustNot (same JSON object): 'The control plane cannot translate provider meaning to resolve a race ... That is the source must-not.' Stated correctly, then excepted four fields later.
measurement.selfContradiction2: $.t1CancellationComposition.join: 'J-1 binds ordering only.' An ordering-only join cannot host a meaning-translation exception.

blockers.secondDefectSameClause: The clause also presupposes an unobservable premise. It directs control-plane behaviour upon 'provider-only in-band Cancel', but under CPC v2's opacity rule the control plane cannot identify any provider frame: content is invisible, and 'The control plane has no concept of a provider duplicate: recognizing one would require reading content.' Recognizing a provider Cancel is the same forbidden read.
blockers.whyBlocker: This is not imprecision - it is an affirmative grant of the exact authority the artifact was rewritten to disclaim. v1 was rejected partly for over-claiming on the must-not; v2 sources the must-not correctly and then reintroduces the escape as an exception clause. Left standing, it licenses the control plane to assign supervision meaning to provider frames during a race, which is the core prohibition of the DR-102/DR-127 demarcation and an 'authority escape' under DR-125's own acceptance cell.
blockers.fix: Delete 'except under the owning J-1 join'. If the intent was that J-1 still ORDERS the events, say that explicitly: 'J-1 appends both events to the merged order; the owning contract alone assigns meaning.' That states the ordering fact without granting translation.

shouldFix.title: A required dual-carrier fanout trigger rests on an invented term and misdescribes the applied provider contract
shouldFix.text: 'host-observed process death that the applied provider contract treats as cancellation-equivalent'

measurement.corpusSearch: 'cancellation-equivalent' occurs in exactly ONE file in docs/: component-sdk-contract.v2.json itself. Zero occurrences in CPC v2, file 02, file 08, delivery.v2/v4, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. The term has no source referent.
measurement.applied contract CancelV1.reason: closed enum 'user-interrupt|host-shutdown' - process death is not a member, so no valid CancelV1 can even be constructed for this trigger.
measurement.applied contract cancelTransition: 'Cancel may be sent once from any NONTERMINAL state; only Cancelled may follow, after which EOF is required.' A dead process is terminal, so the transition is barred by the contract's own state rule, not merely by physics.
measurement.applied contract userCancellation: 'On SIGINT/SIGTERM before finalization, send Cancel once, close the request side, allow the host's bounded cleanup grace, then terminate the child if needed.' Cancel PRECEDES termination; the artifact's item inverts that order.
measurement.CPC v2 teardown ladder: process death is T-5 ('reap and final death event') - the terminus of teardown, not a cancellation initiator.

shouldFix.defect: The item sits in a list of conditions where fanout is REQUIRED, and $.composition.fanout asserts 'Both happen.' For this trigger both cannot happen: no applied provider contract treats death as cancellation-equivalent, and none could accept the frame if it did. The 'IFF ... live in-band Cancel transition' guard in the fanout rule silently evaluates false here, leaving a normative REQUIRED entry that produces no composition - the opposite of the composed-transition repair this section was written to deliver.
shouldFix.note: Filed as SHOULD-FIX rather than BLOCKER because the IFF guard prevents an implementer from actually emitting the forbidden frame. If the coordinator reads the REQUIRED list as normative on its own, it rises to a blocker.
shouldFix.fix: Drop the item, or restate it as what the sources support: on host-observed process death the control plane appends the death boundary event and runs the teardown ladder; no in-band Cancel is sent because the provider transition is unavailable from a terminal state.

summary: v2's honesty repairs are real and independently verified. The D-015 routing claim is gone in every site, the self-granted disposition is downgraded to a PROPOSED composition with the two offending keys deleted, the must-not is now quoted from file 02 word for word, the COORD pin is labelled inherited with an honest live re-measurement (exact at its stated HEAD), and the closed roster holds with no silent v1-to-v2 drift. All three of my v1 findings are repaired. The failure is new, and it is in the repair itself: the dual-carrier composition added for the Codex finding ends with 'except under the owning J-1 join', granting the control plane permission to translate provider meaning into supervision meaning at precisely the race point file 02 forbids - contradicting the artifact's own mustNot and join fields, and presupposing a provider frame the opacity rule forbids it to recognize. A second, softer defect names a required fanout trigger on an invented term ('cancellation-equivalent', found nowhere else in the corpus) that the applied provider contract's closed reason enum and nonterminal-state rule both refuse. Both are narrow and fixable by deletion; neither touches the carried text, which remains impeccable.
